brief: ZeroHedge covers a weekly Goldman custom-baskets note from Louis Miller. Backdrop: only AI and oil are trading right now, so demand for trades uncorrelated to both is high. Goldman's S&P ex-AI basket just had its third-best outperformance day ever against the S&P (+2.2pp) and sits about 5 points ahead of the index over the past year, though Miller cautions a weaker growth outlook would hit ex-AI pockets that rallied mainly on short squeezes. For the midterms, betting markets price a Democratic sweep near 70% (Kalshi now 68%), and Goldman's favorite long is its ACA Beneficiaries basket, betting that reauthorized premium subsidies lift hospital and insurer earnings. That basket has still dropped 7% as odds rose. The article argues the real obstacle is a presidential veto, not House control, since the president let the credits lapse and has vowed to veto Democratic bills, a reading Citi reinforces by expecting any shutdown deal to delay spending cuts rather than add subsidies. Other Goldman ideas: AI Power up, AI hardware ex-Power down, Healthcare AI Beneficiaries and a Growth/Value Rotator as AI-uncorrelated diversifiers, Software vs. Semis and insurers as underpriced AI-disruption plays, and Greek/Japanese banks plus European Defense as rebound trades.
